paulo-morales.text: Says affordability is a top concern: "I will work to lower burdensome taxes and fees, reduce wasteful spending, and support efforts that make life more affordable for working families."
Says the state faces an $18 billion budget shortfall and "we must reevaluate how the government spends money and stop funding programs that do not deliver results."
On housing: cities need flexibility and tools to meet development goals, and state mandates won't succeed without real support; promises "responsible development" and empowering local governments.
On education: will focus on fundamentals, real-world skills and transparency so parents know what children are learning; says families deserve meaningful choices.
Says his law enforcement career showed the importance of trust and accountability; will work for balanced policies that reduce crime and keep neighborhoods safe.

Said: "Do I sometimes think the government as a whole has an overreach problem in controlling us and telling us what to do? Absolutely." He became a Republican in late 2025, after growing up a Democrat.

paulo-morales.text: Spent more than two decades with the Cypress Police Department, including patrol operations and the West Orange County SWAT team, before serving on Cypress city government (former mayor).
